data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The single domain expert remains more reliable because 'trained non-experts' merely simulate the output of expertise without the underlying conceptual model, leading to 'brittle reliability' that fails when the problem deviates slightly from the checklist's assumptions.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task is highly standardized with zero variance in problem structure.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist includes a 'stop-and-escalate' trigger for atypical patterns.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 'Conceptual Model Gap' mechanism: Experts possess a holistic mental model that allows them to recognize when a problem is an 'exception' to the rule; non-experts following a checklist are blind to the boundaries of the tool's applicability, leading to high compliance but catastrophic failure in atypical cases.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
